items.title: Requirements and non-functional requirements
items.overview: Separate functional features from NFRs: scale, latency, availability, durability, consistency, cost, compliance.
items.whyGoogle: Google design interviews grade problem framing before depth.
items.practicePrompt: Attempt without AI: write requirements for a photo sharing app in 10 minutes, then add numbers.

items.title: Back-of-envelope estimation
items.overview: Use powers of two, QPS = DAU * actions / 86400, storage = objects * size * retention.
steps: Derive peak QPS with peak factor
items.youtubeSearch: system design back of envelope estimation
items.whyGoogle: Order-of-magnitude sanity is mandatory at Google scale discussions.
items.practicePrompt: Estimate storage for 500M users posting 1 KB metadata daily for 5 years—solo first.

items.title: API design and idempotency
items.overview: REST or RPC resources with clear verbs, pagination, versioning, and idempotent writes for safe retries.
items.whyGoogle: API clarity reflects how Google ships multi-team platforms.
items.practicePrompt: Design APIs for a task tracker without AI; then review retry behavior.

items.title: Database selection framework
items.overview: Match access patterns: relational for transactions, wide-column/KV for scale, search engines for full text, cache for hot keys.
steps: Pick primary store plus cache/search if needed
checklist: Justify SQL vs NoSQL with patterns
items.whyGoogle: Wrong store choice fails designs quickly in Google loops.
items.practicePrompt: Pick storage for an analytics event pipeline—attempt solo with written trade-offs.

items.title: Caching strategies
items.overview: Cache-aside, write-through, write-back; TTL and invalidation; protect against stampede with locking or request coalescing.
steps: Identify hot keys and hit ratio goal
Plan for cold start and thundering herd
items.whyGoogle: Caching is the default lever for Google-scale read-heavy systems.
items.practicePrompt: Add cache to a read-heavy profile service design; attempt without AI first.

items.title: Sharding and consistent hashing
items.overview: Partition data by key; consistent hashing minimizes remapping on node changes; virtual nodes balance load.
steps: Pick shard key for even spread
items.whyGoogle: Sharding appears in most high-scale Google design prompts.
items.practicePrompt: Shard a user timeline store—write approach before viewing any solution.

items.title: Message queues and async processing
items.overview: Decouple producers/consumers; at-least-once delivery with idempotent consumers; dead-letter queues for poison messages.
checklist: Compare sync vs async user experience
items.whyGoogle: Async pipelines power Search indexing, ads, and analytics at Google.
items.practicePrompt: Design email send pipeline async—attempt solo, then compare delivery guarantees.

items.title: Observability: metrics, logs, traces
items.overview: Golden signals: latency, traffic, errors, saturation. Structured logs and distributed traces for debugging.
items.whyGoogle: Google SRE culture expects operability in design answers.
items.practicePrompt: List SLIs for a payment API without AI assistance first.

items.title: High-level design: URL shortener
items.overview: Generate short codes, redirect with low latency, analytics optional, high read QPS vs moderate writes.
steps: Choose base62 ID generation vs hash
Store mapping in KV/SQL with cache
checklist: Cache hot links at CDN edge
items.whyGoogle: Canonical warm-up HLD—interviewers probe scaling and collision handling.
items.practicePrompt: Full 35-minute HLD on whiteboard; attempt without AI until debrief.

items.title: High-level design: Rate limiter
items.overview: Enforce per-user/IP limits globally in distributed system using token bucket and shared store.
steps: Define limit dimensions (user, IP, API key)
Handle clock skew and race conditions
checklist: Fail open vs closed on store outage
items.whyGoogle: Protects Google APIs—common LLD/HLD hybrid question.
items.practicePrompt: Design global 1000 req/min per API key limiter solo first.

items.title: High-level design: News feed
items.overview: Fan-out on write vs fan-out on read for home timeline; celebrity user problem; ranking optional.
steps: Choose fan-out strategy with scale math
items.whyGoogle: Social graph products mirror Google-adjacent scale thinking.
items.practicePrompt: Design Instagram-style feed for 10M DAU—no AI until after first draft.

items.title: High-level design: Chat messaging
items.overview: Real-time delivery, message ordering per conversation, presence, offline sync, media attachments.
items.whyGoogle: Real-time systems test WebSockets, storage, and consistency choices.
items.practicePrompt: 45-minute chat HLD with 1:1 and group rooms—attempt independently.

items.title: High-level design: Notification system
items.overview: Multi-channel delivery (push, email, SMS), templates, user preferences, deduplication, priority queues.
items.whyGoogle: Cross-product notifications resemble Google-wide platforms.
items.practicePrompt: Design notifications for e-commerce order updates without AI first.

items.title: High-level design: File storage (Dropbox-like)
items.overview: Upload/download large files, deduplication via chunking, metadata DB, sync across devices.
checklist: Encrypt at rest and in transit
items.whyGoogle: Storage + metadata split mirrors Google Drive components conceptually.
items.practicePrompt: HLD file sync for 100GB user quota—solo attempt with diagram.

items.title: High-level design: Search autocomplete
items.overview: Low-latency prefix suggestions from aggregated query logs; trie or specialized index; personalization optional.
items.whyGoogle: Directly related to Google Search product thinking.
items.practicePrompt: Design autocomplete for 1B queries/day—attempt without references first.

items.title: High-level design: Distributed job queue
items.overview: Workers pull jobs with visibility timeout, retries, priorities, scheduling, and exactly-once illusion via idempotency.
items.whyGoogle: Batch and async compute underpin Google infrastructure.
items.practicePrompt: Design video transcoding queue—write flows before AI review.

items.title: Low-level design: Parking lot
items.overview: Classic OOD: vehicles, spots, tickets, pricing rules—practice encapsulation and extensibility.
checklist: Open for extension on vehicle types
items.whyGoogle: LLD rounds test clean class design without distributed noise.
items.practicePrompt: Implement parking lot classes in Go or Java—attempt without AI first.

items.title: Low-level design: In-memory rate limiter class
items.overview: Single-process token bucket with thread-safe API—bridge to distributed version later.
steps: Store buckets per key in map
Refill tokens based on elapsed time
Unit test time advancement with fake clock
checklist: Bound memory with LRU of keys
items.youtubeSearch: rate limiter low level design coding
items.whyGoogle: Often paired with Go/Java coding in Google onsite loops.
items.practicePrompt: Code token bucket in Go with tests—no AI until tests fail twice.

items.title: Low-level design: LRU cache
items.overview: O(1) get/put using hash map + doubly linked list—frequent coding prompt.
steps: Update on get to mark recent
items.whyGoogle: Data structure + OOD combo mirrors coding depth expectations.
items.practicePrompt: Implement LRU from scratch timed 25 minutes without AI.

items.title: Consistency models in design
items.overview: Strong, eventual, causal; read-your-writes and monotonic reads for UX; pick per use case.
steps: Use version vectors or timestamps if needed
items.whyGoogle: Google Spanner and global DBs make consistency a favorite topic.
items.practicePrompt: Pick consistency for shopping cart vs product catalog—justify solo.

items.title: Leader election and failover
items.overview: Use coordination service (etcd/ZooKeeper) or DB leases for single writer; fencing tokens prevent stale leaders.
items.whyGoogle: Reliability of primary services depends on clean failover stories.
items.practicePrompt: Design failover for a cron scheduler leader—attempt without AI.

items.title: Multi-region active-active
items.overview: Geo routing, replicated data, conflict resolution, and compliance with data residency.
items.youtubeSearch: multi region active active system design
items.whyGoogle: Google runs globally—candidates should discuss region failure.
items.practicePrompt: Extend URL shortener to two regions—solo draft first.

items.title: Search index pipeline
items.overview: Crawl/ingest → parse → index inverted → serve queries with ranking signals offline/online.
items.whyGoogle: Search heritage makes indexing pipelines a credible deep dive.
items.practicePrompt: Outline index pipeline for product catalog search—no AI initially.

items.title: Video streaming architecture
items.overview: Upload, transcode ladder, CDN delivery, adaptive bitrate playback, view counts.
items.whyGoogle: YouTube-scale thinking tests media pipelines and CDN usage.
items.practicePrompt: Design Netflix-like streaming HLD in 40 minutes solo.

items.title: Payment system sketch
items.overview: Strong consistency for balances, idempotent payments, ledger, reconciliation, PCI scope minimization.
items.whyGoogle: Correctness and auditability mirror Google Wallet/Ads billing rigor.
items.practicePrompt: Design charge API with webhook confirmation—attempt without AI.

items.title: Low-level design: Elevator system
items.overview: Dispatch algorithm, elevator state, requests queue—OOD and concurrency discussion.
items.whyGoogle: Tests structured thinking beyond CRUD APIs.
items.practicePrompt: Code elevator dispatcher for 3 cars—solo attempt first.

items.title: Bloom filters and count-min sketch
items.overview: Probabilistic structures save memory for membership and frequency approximations with tunable error rates.
steps: Size bloom filter from m, k, n
Combine with exact store on hit
items.whyGoogle: Bigtable/Search culture uses probabilistic structures routinely.
items.practicePrompt: Explain where to put bloom filter in URL shortener—write solo.

items.title: Capacity planning and load testing
items.overview: Load test critical paths, find knee in latency curve, plan headroom for launches and failover.
steps: Add capacity or optimize hot path
items.whyGoogle: Launch readiness reviews expect measurement, not guesses.
items.practicePrompt: Plan load test for feed read API—outline solo before AI.

items.title: Security in system design
items.overview: Authentication, authorization, encryption, secrets management, audit logs, threat modeling STRIDE lightly.
items.whyGoogle: Security is non-negotiable for user data at Google scale.
items.practicePrompt: Threat-model file storage design for insider abuse—solo first.

items.title: Wrap-up and deep-dive selection
items.overview: Reserve 5 minutes to summarize; invite interviewer to deep dive on bottleneck, failure, or scaling dimension.
steps: Quantify again if new constraint added
checklist: Do not introduce new scope late
items.whyGoogle: Strong candidates drive the interview collaboratively.
items.practicePrompt: Practice 60-second recap for news feed design—record without AI.
